openwrt_git.commit_message:
mpc85xx: add support for Hewlett Packard MSM460

Hardware
--------
CPU:  Freescale P1020 2xe500 PPC
RAM:  256M DDR3 (Micron MT41J64M16JT-15E:G "D9MNJ")
NAND: 128M (Micron 2CA1)
BTN:  1x Reset
LED:  Power - ETH - Radio1 - Radio2
UART: RJ-45 Cisco Pinout - 115200 8N1

Installation
------------
NOTE: You can find a repo with up-to-date instructions as well as
the required files here:

https://github.com/blocktrron/msm460-flashing

Required files
==============
You need a command-files as well as a U-Boot image.

The command-file has the following content (padded to 131072 bytes).

If you copy paste these, remove the newlines!

```
U-BOOT setenv ethaddr 02:03:04:05:06:07; setenv ipaddr 192.168.1.1;
setenv serverip 192.168.1.66; tftpboot 0x3000000 msm460-uboot.bin;
nand device; nand erase 0 0xC0000; nand write 0x3000000 0x0 0xC0000; reset
```

You can download the required U-Boot from this repository:

https://github.com/blocktrron/u-boot-msm/releases

Preparation
===========
Prepare a TFTP server serving two files:

 - U-Boot NAND image as `msm460-uboot.bin`.
 - OpenWrt factory image as `msm460-factory.bin`
 - Command-file names `commands.tftp`

You can start a TFTP server in the current directory using dnsmasq:

```bash
sudo dnsmasq --no-daemon --listen-address=0.0.0.0 \
    --port=0 --enable-tftp=enxd0 --tftp-root="$(pwd)" \
    --user=root --group=root
```
Replace `enxd0` with the name of your network interface.

Procedure
=========
1. Assign yourself the IP-Address 192.168.1.66/24.
3. Connect the Router to the PC while keeping the reset button
   pressed.
4. The LEDs will eventually begin to flash.
   They will start to flash faster after around 15 seconds.
5. Release the reset button.
6. Start a new shell
7. Make sure you are currently in the directory where the tftp server
   is located.
8. Run the following command:

```bash
tftp 192.168.1.1 -m binary -c put commands.tftp nflashd.cccc9999
```

You get the message "Transfer timed out."
To find out if you have been successful, please check the
blinking LED Pattern.

Signed-off-by: David Bauer <mail@david-bauer.net>

deviwiki._text:
[http://h17007.www1.hp.com/us/en/products/wireless/HP_E-802_11n_Dual_Radio_Access_Point_Series/index.aspx Product page]
[http://content.etilize.com/User-Manual/1019134534.pdf Quick-start guide] The same hardware is (probably) used for the E-MSM430, E-MSM460, and E-MSM466. The MSM430 is a two-stream only device (integral antennas?). The MSM460 is dual-band 3x3:3 capable with integral antenans. The MSM466 is dual-band 3x3:3 device (multi-5GHz capable) with RP-SMA connectors. "5184-5953", "(C)Copyright 2010 Hewlett-Packard Development Company, L.P.", and "[G]48RNAA0P.SGC" is silkscreened on the board. '''Wistron NeWeb''' is the presumed manufacturer. The wireless modules are silkscreened with "(XB114_030)", "2010/05/31", "4BDNXA07.SGB". This matches with Unex's ( / '''Wistron NeWeb''''s) [http://www.unex.com.tw/product/dnxa-h1 DNXA-H1]. Three '''SiGe''' SE2595L frontends are used per card. The CPU may be a Freescale chip (P1020PSE2HPA).

{{TagLine|Dual Radio 802.11n AP (AM)}}
:[https://www.hpe.com/psnow/doc/c04915279 Product page] {{•}} [https://support.hpe.com/hpesc/public/docDisplay?docId=c03127714&docLocale=en_US Quick-start Guide]

"5185-8967", "©2010 Hewlett-Packard Development Company, L.P.", 
:"[G]48RNAA0P.OGC" and "2011/07/15" are silkscreened on the board. 
 
"48DNXA07.OGB", "(XB114_030)", "2011/04/13" is silkscreened 
:on the wireless modules ([[Atheros]] XB114 reference design).

This matches with [[Unex]]'s ( / ''[[Wistron NeWeb]]'''s) [http://www.unex.com.tw/product/dnxa-h1 DNXA-H1]. 
:Three ''[[SiGe]]'' SE2595L Front-ends (FEM) are used per card.

* WLAN Radio Module - Model: [[HP MRLBB-1003]]
{{See also|HP MRLBB-1301}}

The CPU is a [[Freescale]] chip (P1020 PSE2HPA).
:''[[Wistron NeWeb]]'' is the presumed manufacturer.
{{See also|Aerohive HiveAP 330|Aerohive HiveAP 350}}

The same hardware is used for the MSM430, MSM460, and MSM466.
*The MSM430 is a two-stream only device (integral antennas). 
*The MSM460 is dual-band 3x3:3 capable with integral antennas. 
*The MSM466 is dual-band 3x3:3 device (multi-5GHz capable) 
:with RP-SMA connectors.

This entry is for the Americas version of the device
:there are also other area specific versions available
:J9591A (World-wide), J9589A (Japan), J9618A (Israel)

===Hardware specification===
*CPU: ''[[Freescale]]'' ([[NXP]]) P1020 @667MHz
:SoC: Dual-core ''PowerPC'' e500
*Flash: 128MB (NAND) Flash
*Memory: 256MB (DDR3) SDRAM
*Wi-Fi: [[Atheros]] AR9390
:802.11abgn (2.4GHz) 3x3:3
:[[Atheros]] AR9390
:802.11an (5GHz) 3x3:3
*Network: 1x GbE port 
*Power Source: 802.3af PoE
